summary: An MBW Trailblazers interview with Abdul Karim Abdullah, Co-Founder and CEO of Ghana-based AfroFuture (formerly Afrochella), covering the festival's growth from 4,600 attendees in 2017 to 31,000 in 2022. He discusses the audience, the Rising Star Challenge, tourism impact, the AfroFuture Foundation's philanthropy, and expansion plans via 'Road to AfroFuture'. The piece sits against the backdrop of Sub-Saharan Africa being the world's fastest-growing recorded music region in 2022.
one_line: AfroFuture CEO Abdul Karim Abdullah explains how the Accra festival formerly known as Afrochella grew into a pan-African culture brand with tourism, talent and philanthropy arms.
key_facts: Sub-Saharan Africa was the world's fastest-growing recorded music region in 2022, with 34.7% YoY growth (IFPI).
Mdundo reported a 239% YoY jump in revenue from paid subscriptions and a 23.2% YoY increase in monthly active users.
AfroFuture, formerly Afrochella, launched in Accra on December 29, 2017 at the Accra Polo Court, attracting 4,600 attendees.
The sixth annual festival, held at EL Wak Stadium at the end of December 2022, drew 31,000 attendees over two days, with Burna Boy and Stonebwoy headlining.
Abdul Karim Abdullah, who grew up in the Bronx, co-founded AfroFuture with Kenny Agyapong after a visit to Ghana.
The vision is to bring African art, cuisine, fashion, and music to a global audience.
About 45% of the audience comes from North America, 13% from Europe and Asia, and about 12% from African countries outside Ghana and South Africa; attendees represent over 40 countries.
The Rising Star Challenge selects 10 musicians from a shortlist of 25, then five finalists perform on the Rising Star Stage; the winner gets a single deal with Sony Music Africa.
In 2022, the Rising Star DJ Challenge was added in partnership with TuneCore, with three finalists competing at the AfroFuture Music Museum in Accra on December 27.
In 2019, AfroFuture helped bring in $2.1 billion in tourism revenue for 'Year of Return', and the festival is expected to generate about 16% of Ghana's tourism this year.
The founders were named Goodwill Ambassador of Tourism to Ghana.
Road to AfroFuture, launched in 2022, has expanded to the UK, South Africa, Côte d'Ivoire, and France.
AfroFuture Feeds raised over $5,000 to feed 500 families, and drew over 250 volunteers in 2022.
South Africa events drew over 1,000 attendees in 2022 and 2023; in New York AfroFuture partners with Positive Vibes Only and Days Like This.
This year's December edition is headlined by Davido and J-Hus.
